NC500 in 5 Days: The Sweet Spot

Five days is the Goldilocks duration for the NC500 by motorcycle. It gives you enough time to explore the highlights, take scenic detours, and still maintain a comfortable daily mileage of around 100 miles. You'll have time for photography, walking, and enjoying Scotland's legendary hospitality.

Day 1: Inverness to Wick (110 miles)

Head north on the A9 along the east coast. This is the gentlest section of the NC500 and a good warm-up day. The Moray Firth coastline is home to dolphins, and Dunrobin Castle is worth a stop. Arrive in Wick with plenty of daylight left to explore the harbour.

  • Dunrobin Castle — Scotland's fairy-tale castle with falconry displays
  • Brora — Fuel stop and a stretch of beautiful coastline
  • Overnight in Wick — Mackays Hotel has bike parking

Day 2: Wick to Durness (105 miles)

Cross the top of Britain along the north coast. John o' Groats is the famous landmark but the real riding pleasure is the A836 west towards Thurso and on to Durness. The coastline is raw and windswept — properly dramatic stuff.

Day 3: Durness to Ullapool (95 miles)

The shortest day on paper, but the most photogenic. The road south from Durness through Kylesku and Lochinver is where the NC500 truly comes alive. Every bend reveals a new loch, mountain, or sea inlet. Take your time.

Day 3 is where the NC500 goes from 'very good' to 'life-changing'. Resist the urge to rush — every mile deserves your full attention.

Day 4: Ullapool to Applecross (90 miles)

Head south and make the detour to Applecross via the Bealach na Bà. This is the highlight of the entire route — a genuine Alpine-style pass with hairpin bends and 20% gradients. The descent towards Applecross with Skye in the distance is breathtaking. Stay in Applecross — the inn serves excellent seafood and local ales.

Day 5: Applecross to Inverness (115 miles)

Leave Applecross via the coast road north to Shieldaig (stunning single-track), then pick up the A896 through Torridon and Glen Carron. Join the A87 at Invergarry and cruise east back to Inverness. A perfect final day blending coastal and glen riding.

5-Day Budget Guide

Expect to spend around £80-120 per night on accommodation (B&B or small hotel). Fuel will cost roughly £50-70 total depending on your bike. Budget £25-35 per day for food if eating at pubs and cafes. The NC500 is not a budget trip, but it's worth every penny. Wild camping is legal in Scotland and can dramatically reduce costs if you carry the right gear.
keyTakeaways: Five days is the sweet spot, with comfortable daily mileage of around 100 miles.
Day 1 heads north on the A9 to Wick, a gentle warm-up past Dunrobin Castle and the Moray Firth.
Day 3 from Durness to Ullapool is the shortest at 95 miles but the most photogenic.
Day 4 includes the Bealach na Ba detour to Applecross, the highlight of the whole route.
Budget roughly 80 to 120 pounds per night for accommodation, with wild camping legal in Scotland to cut costs.

faq.q: Why is five days the ideal NC500 duration?
faq.a: Five days gives enough time to explore highlights, take scenic detours and still keep a comfortable daily mileage of around 100 miles. You gain time for photography, walking and Highland hospitality without the constant rush of a three-day dash, which is why many riders consider it the Goldilocks duration.

faq.q: Which is the best day of the 5-day route?
faq.a: Day three from Durness to Ullapool is the shortest at 95 miles but the most photogenic, where the NC500 goes from very good to life-changing. Day four is arguably the highlight, with the Bealach na Ba detour to Applecross delivering a genuine Alpine-style pass and views to Skye.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a 5-day NC500?
faq.a: Expect around 80 to 120 pounds per night for a B&B or small hotel, roughly 50 to 70 pounds total on fuel depending on your bike, and 25 to 35 pounds per day for food at pubs and cafes. Wild camping is legal in Scotland and can dramatically reduce costs.

faq.q: Where is the best overnight stop for the Bealach na Ba?
faq.a: Stay in Applecross at the end of day four. The Applecross Inn serves excellent seafood and local ales, and basing yourself there means you can enjoy the pass without rushing. The following morning you leave via the stunning single-track coast road north to Shieldaig.
